title: Unramifiedness of a group algebraic space is detected along its identity
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $B$ be an algebraic space over $S$, and let $q:G\to B$ be locally of finite type. Suppose $G$ is a group algebraic space over $B$: it has multiplication $G\times_B G\to G$, identity section $e:B\to G$, and inverse $G\to G$, satisfying the group identities on every test scheme. Then $q$ is unramified if and only if $q$ is unramified at $e(b)$ for every $b\in|B|$. Algebraic spaces and their morphisms use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Their fibre products and point sets $|X|$ (field-valued points up to common field extension) use [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Locally of finite type and unramified for algebraic spaces are tested etale locally on source and target with [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-unramified-morphism]. An open subspace is an inclusion whose every scheme base change is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. A morphism is unramified at a point if some open neighbourhood of that point has unramified restriction.

proof.text: Let $W=U(q)\subseteq G$ be the largest unramified open supplied by [lem-sfb-space-unramified-locus-base-change], applicable since $q$ is locally of finite type. Its points are precisely those where $q$ is unramified, and its formation commutes with every base change on $B$. If $q$ is unramified then $W=G$, so in particular every $e(b)$ lies in $W$. For the converse assume that every $e(b)$ belongs to $W$.

Fix $x\in|G|$. By the description of points in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], choose a representative $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to G$ and put $h=q\circ g$. Form $H=G\times_B\operatorname{Spec}K$. Its group operations are obtained by applying the given operations to pairs with equal image in $B$; the group identities hold on every test scheme. The pair $(g,\mathrm{id})$ is a $K$-point $\widetilde g$ of $H$. For $p:H\to G$, the locus theorem gives $U(H/\operatorname{Spec}K)=p^{-1}(W)$. Its identity $e_K$ maps to $e(h(*))\in W$, so it lies in this locus. These are arbitrary field-valued points; no rationality assumption on $x$ over its image in $B$ is made.

For each $K$-scheme $T$, define $\tau_{\widetilde g}(a)=\widetilde g_Ta$ on $H(T)$. These maps are natural in $T$, hence give a morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The group identities give inverse $a\mapsto\widetilde g_T^{-1}a$ and $\tau_{\widetilde g}(e_K)=\widetilde g$. This is an automorphism over $K$. Unramifiedness at a point is unchanged under this automorphism: an open neighbourhood $V$ of $e_K$ corresponds isomorphically to the open neighbourhood $\tau_{\widetilde g}(V)$ of $\widetilde g$; composing its etale scheme charts with this isomorphism gives exactly the same scheme structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Thus the chart test for unramifiedness [def-weil-unramified-morphism] is identical. Consequently $\widetilde g\in U(H/\operatorname{Spec}K)$.

The equality $U(H/\operatorname{Spec}K)=p^{-1}(W)$ and $p(\widetilde g)=x$ now imply $x\in W$. Since $x$ was arbitrary, $|W|=|G|$. An open subspace with every point is the whole space: on each scheme chart its pullback is an open subscheme containing every point and hence is that scheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus $W=G$, and the defining property of $W$ proves that $q$ is unramified.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q107-42835770a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and its four steps in full. Read Stacks 0DSI (spaces-groupoids lemma-group-scheme-unramified-or-lqf; tag confirmed in tags/tags) and 05W2 (spaces-morphisms lemma-where-unramified) at source. The item statement matches the 0DSI unramified clause hypothesis by hypothesis (S scheme, B space, G a group space, q locally of finite type, iff unramified at e(b) for all b in |B|), and it is not weakened. Step 1 uses the statement of lem-sfb-space-unramified-locus-base-change: a largest open, the pointwise description and the base-change equality; that node is unsplit with no proof_deps, so there is no cycle. Step 2 forms H = G x_B Spec K by lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers; the fibrewise group law, the K-point g~=(g,id), e_K mapping to e([h]) in W and U(H/K) = H x_G W are all correct, and the uncited fact that points of H x_G W are the points mapping into |W| is a few lines from the point description, so I accept it as elementary. Step 3 writes out left translation and its inverse explicitly; it is natural in T, lies over K and sends e_K to g~, and the étale-local unramified test is invariant under an isomorphism over K; commutativity is not needed. Step 4: p(g~)=x gives |W|=|G|, and an open subscheme of every scheme T containing all points is T, so W=G and q is unramified. Duplicate search over the snapshot DAG found only 0DSJ base-locus (cites this item, correctly not used), the group-scheme dual-number criterion, pseudo-torsor and atlas-diagonal nodes, none of them the same statement. Accepted tool use: lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers as generic infrastructure. No SGA citations. Edge cases checked: empty B, G_a, mu_p in characteristic p, constant étale group, noncommutative G. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem groupSpace_unramified_iff_identity {S : Scheme.{u}} (B G : AlgebraicSpace S) (q : G ⟶ B) (group : @GrpObj (Over B.obj) inferInstance (Over.cartesianMonoidalCategory B.obj) (Over.mk q.hom)) (hq : MapIsLocally (@LocallyOfFiniteType) q) : MapIsLocally (@AlgebraicGeometry.IsUnramified) q ↔ ∀ b : Point B.obj.obj, ∃ (V : AlgebraicSpace S) (i : V ⟶ G), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) i.hom.hom ∧ mapPoint group.one.left.hom b ∈ pointImage i.hom.hom ∧ MapIsLocally (@AlgebraicGeometry.IsUnramified) (i ≫ q)
